04 // hands-on work
Projects & Hands-On Experience
Project 4: Wireshark Attack PCAP Analysis
CYBEROPS

Analyzed a packet capture file to identify a TCP SYN scan attack originating from 192.168.56.10 targeting 192.168.56.20. Identified that repeated SYN packets with no corresponding SYN-ACK responses revealed reconnaissance activity rather than legitimate communication, indicating an attacker mapping open ports before exploitation.

Wireshark PCAP Analysis TCP/IP Protocols Threat Hunting

What I learned: Traffic patterns across multiple packets reveal attacker behavior far more than any single packet. PCAP analysis provides critical forensic evidence during incident response, helping analysts understand, contain, and prevent attacks. This lab reinforced that identifying incomplete TCP handshakes is a key indicator of SYN-based reconnaissance.

[ Project 4 screenshots — paste Wireshark captures here ]
Project 6: Windows System Hardening
CYBEROPS

Applied a series of Windows security hardening configurations to reduce the attack surface of a live system. Tasks included enabling PUA protection, activating Tamper Protection, configuring service startup types, enforcing screen timeout policies, and verifying Windows Firewall was active across all network profiles (public, private, and domain).

Windows Security Windows Firewall Tamper Protection Group Policy System Hardening

What I learned: System hardening is critical even when no attack is visible — many threats aren't immediately detectable. Attackers often exploit weak configurations silently. Verifying that the firewall is active across all network profiles reduces unauthorized access risk by blocking unwanted connections and preventing exploitation of open ports or unpatched vulnerabilities.

[ Project 6 screenshots — PUA protection, Tamper Protection, Firewall configs ]

XP Cyber Challenge: Preventative Protection – Thwarting the Imminent Threat
XP CYBER

Responded to an anonymous tip that a system was under imminent outside attack. Deployed defensive measures on a Domain Controller before the attack could be completed. Passed both automated checks — Domain-Controller Host Check and Attack Thwarted — achieving a full 2/2 pass in just 44 seconds. Submission ID: 153460 · Completed: 3/24/2026.

XP Cyber Range Active Directory Incident Response Domain Controller Hardening

What I learned: Cyber defense requires speed and precision. This challenge reinforced real-time incident response skills — particularly the importance of quickly validating host integrity and deploying countermeasures under pressure. It also aligned with DCWF Task 762: performing real-time cyber defense incident handling to support deployable Incident Response Teams.

Splunk SIEM: EventCode Investigation (Event Code 1)
NDG LAB

Used Splunk Enterprise 10.2.0 to query Windows Sysmon logs and investigate Event Code 1 (process creation) events. Executed a search across all sourcetypes filtered by EventCode, returning 93 matched events. Analyzed XML-formatted Sysmon entries to identify process execution details including image paths, parent processes, command-line arguments, and user context on the host "Bryan".

Splunk Enterprise 10.2.0 Sysmon Windows Event Logs SPL (Search Processing Language) SIEM Analysis

What I learned: Splunk's SPL queries are a powerful way to surface suspicious process creation events at scale. Sysmon Event Code 1 logs provide rich forensic detail — hashes, parent process chains, command-line arguments — making them invaluable for detecting malware execution and living-off-the-land attacks in a SOC environment.

05 // growth
Reflections & Lessons Learned
⚡
Skills Gained

On the technical side, I became comfortable using Wireshark for packet analysis, Nmap for network reconnaissance, Metasploit for understanding exploit frameworks, and Splunk for SIEM log investigation. Professionally, I developed strong documentation skills — writing reports clear enough that anyone, regardless of technical background, can understand what happened and why it matters. I also grew in risk communication, log analysis, and incident reaction. Competing in NCL team games taught me the real value of coordinating with teammates toward a shared goal under pressure.

🔧
Challenges Faced

One recurring challenge was patience. Tools and programs crash — sometimes at the worst moments — and there were times I wanted to give up. I learned to stick it out, because with enough persistence things always got figured out. That mindset shift was as important as any technical skill I developed. Patience turned out to be one of the most underrated virtues in cybersecurity work.

🌐
Growing Understanding

Before this program, I thought cybersecurity was simply about defending against threats. I now understand it's far broader. We can never be 100% safe — every new update or tool introduces potential vulnerabilities, and staying ahead means constantly tracking emerging attacks. I also learned that we don't have to wait for threat actors to test us. By building controlled environments like sandboxes, we can proactively simulate and study attacks to strengthen our defenses before real ones arrive.

🎯
Areas to Improve

I want to get more fluent with CLI commands across key tools, and deepen my familiarity with Kali Linux commands for penetration testing workflows. The command line is where real efficiency lives, and I know becoming faster and more confident there will make me significantly more effective. I'm actively working on this through hands-on practice.
